video_title: How to Find the Next 10x Stock Before Everyone Else
gist: Eric Jackson (EMJ Capital) at a retail-investor event explains his AI-assisted research, his bullish thesis that Hut 8's debt-funded Riverbend data center campus is a misunderstood stock, his concentrated small-cap and crypto portfolio, and his Bitcoin regime model and prediction-market mispricing tool. The title promises a '10x stock' framework; the content is mostly Hut 8/Opendoor conviction and process.

insights.claim: Public company CEOs increasingly ask how to engage retail investors, and Eric Jackson says simple steps like video earnings calls instead of audio-only calls are an easy way to appear human and transparent.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Companies with open retail engagement may build more loyal shareholder bases.

insights.claim: Despite AI lowering the cost of researching companies, retail activism still needs a human leader to step up and organize; it does not emerge automatically from the crowd.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Watch for named retail leaders and campaigns, not just sentiment, as catalysts.
insights.quote: leadership matters online, too. Just because AI is great doesn't mean that things automatically happen.

insights.claim: Pompliano argues retail investors have been right more often than wrong and Wall Street is now waking up to having to follow retail, which is the opposite of the old narrative.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano (host)
insights.so_what: Retail-favored names may get institutional attention later.

insights.claim: Simplistic AI prompts like 'show me the next Carvana' waste tokens and yield little; AI is more valuable for comparative questions on how competing companies in a space differ and why one has an advantage.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Use AI to unpack competitive differentiation within a crowded sector rather than for stock picking.

insights.claim: Jackson finds different LLMs suit different tasks: ChatGPT is most 'artistic' for tweets and PowerPoints, Claude a good workhorse, and Kimi surprisingly best for coding and website redesign.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Match model to task when building a research workflow.

insights.claim: Jackson uses AI each morning to interpret moves in the 10-year yield and ask how a rapid rise affects his holdings such as Opendoor and Hut 8.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Rates sensitivity is a key lens for his small-cap growth portfolio.

insights.claim: Touring Hut 8's 649-acre Riverbend campus north of Baton Rouge showed Jackson the scale of power infrastructure (huge transformers and substations) needed for AI data centers, which he says changed how he understood Hut 8 versus peers like IREN, Nebius and CoreWeave.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Physical diligence reveals execution capability that press releases do not.

insights.claim: Building AI campuses is a coordination challenge across contractors, cooling, power and labor, not cookie-cutter, and Jackson thinks Hut 8 could be best at this 'coordination game' of lighting up megawatts then gigawatts economically.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Execution speed on campus build-out is the differentiator to monitor.

insights.claim: Hut 8 raised about $3.5 billion of non-recourse debt for Riverbend rather than diluting shareholders, in contrast to other players doing roughly $6 billion equity offerings.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Debt-funded build-outs preserve per-share value if execution holds.

insights.claim: Jackson estimates Riverbend needs roughly $10 billion of borrowing, backed by Google financial backstop, Fluidstack and Anthropic as anchor tenant, and that once lit it creates about $15 billion of extra value that can fund the next project (Beacon Point in East Texas).
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Recycling value created per campus into the next is the model's compounding engine.
insights.quote: my calculations are they probably have created like a $15 billion of e extra value that didn't exist before.

insights.claim: Jackson calls Hut 8 one of the most misunderstood stocks, noting misunderstood stories were what Carvana and Opendoor had in common before multi-year runs; CEO Asher Genoot (32) is little known.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Misunderstood-stock pattern is the basis for his long position.

insights.claim: At the Riverbend event, local politicians including the governor and Donald Trump Jr. were enthusiastic, contrasting with the national narrative that communities hate and ban AI data centers.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Local political support in places like Louisiana may ease permitting for data center developers.

insights.claim: United Rentals and Caterpillar benefit visibly from data center construction, which Jackson says explains why their stocks are way up over five years.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Equipment rental and heavy machinery are picks-and-shovels plays on the build-out.

insights.claim: Conviction in contrarian ideas comes from trial and error; you must accept being wrong or too early sometimes.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Size positions assuming timing errors.

insights.claim: Jackson's Opendoor position ran from about 70 cents to nearly $11 last September, then the stock struggled; he believes nothing is wrong with the company or CEO Kaz Nejatian and the sector selloff, tied to rising 10-year yields, unfairly punished it.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Rate-driven drawdowns in a fundamentally intact name may be a re-entry point.

insights.claim: The early-2026 'SaaS is dead' consensus was partly wrong: CrowdStrike was up 125% and Twilio up 100% on the year while ZoomInfo fell sharply, showing the opportunity was sorting real winners when everyone was on one side of the boat.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Sector-wide capitulation creates stock-specific opportunities.
insights.quote: everybody got to one side of the boat

insights.claim: Jackson runs a concentrated, high-risk portfolio weighted toward small-cap growth names such as Hut 8, Opendoor, Nextdoor and Dave, plus crypto, which he says is about 90% of what he plays.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Illustrates a high-beta retail-favored basket.

insights.claim: His biggest investing mistake is being too early to a story; he now asks whether a company is about to inflect, for example revenue growth accelerating from 10% to 30%.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Timing the inflection matters as much as the thesis.

insights.claim: As an optimist he tends to hold too long, so he sells by asking whether management quality or the story changed materially, and whether a miss was a blip or the start of something worse.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Use explicit thesis-change checks to counter bias.

themes.theme: Bitcoin regime model and prediction markets

insights.claim: Jackson sold his Bitcoin AI regime model to SRXH, which plans to turn it into an ETF; it classifies Bitcoin as bull, mixed/choppy or bear/stress and gives about 30 days advance notice of regime flips.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: A regime-signal ETF could become a tradable Bitcoin overlay.

insights.claim: The model flagged stress on May 26 with Bitcoin near 77K (it hit about 58K six weeks later), flipped back to mixed on August 14 at about 62K before a run to 87K, then returned to stress around 84K a week before the talk.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Track record shows early exits and re-entries; currently in stress per the speaker.
insights.quote: it said, "Oh, we're back into a mixed market all all aboard."

insights.claim: Jackson says AI models help remove human emotion from trading, noting that he himself would have said there were no warning signs at 84K Bitcoin the week before the model flagged stress.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Systematic signals can offset optimism bias.

insights.claim: Jackson's Event Horizon site uses AI models to find mispriced Kalshi and Polymarket predictions; on August 12 Polymarket gave 3% odds Bitcoin would end August at 70K, and it ended at 79K.
insights.speaker: Eric Jackson
insights.so_what: Prediction-market odds can be mispriced and exploitable with models.
insights.quote: So the wisdom of crowds is not always correct.
